simple: A program that knows how all the files of a project fit together and runs the right compiler commands, in the right order, only when needed.
analogy: The kitchen's prep plan on the wall.
precise: A tool that reads a description of build targets, their sources and their dependencies, and executes the commands that bring outdated outputs up to date (here CMake generating Makefiles for GNU Make).
source: D1 of F2-26, D3 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A tool that reads your project description and writes the detailed build instructions for another tool.
analogy: The person who turns the menu into a prep plan for this particular kitchen.
precise: A build-system generator: it reads CMakeLists.txt, detects the compiler (configure step), writes native build files for a chosen generator (generate step) and can drive the build and the tests; version 3.28.3 in this build.
source: D1 of F2-26, R1 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One thing the build makes, such as a program or a library.
analogy: One dish or one component on the prep plan.
precise: A named build product created by add_executable or add_library, with its own sources and its own properties (include directories, compile options, linked libraries).
source: D1 of F2-26, R7 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The kind of build instructions CMake writes.
analogy: Writing the prep plan in the language of this kitchen's staff.
precise: The back end that CMake writes files for; in this build the default "Unix Makefiles" generator, whose build ran /usr/bin/gmake.
source: D1 of F2-26, R9 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A named set of compiler settings, such as one for debugging and one for speed.
analogy: A practice service (slow, everything checked) versus the real dinner service.
precise: The value of CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE on single-configuration generators, with typical values Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo and MinSizeRel; in this build Debug added -g and Release added -O3 -DNDEBUG.
source: R7 of F2-26, R4 of F2-26, R9 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Putting everything the build makes in a separate folder, so your source folder stays clean.
analogy: Preparing on a separate counter, not on top of the recipe book.
precise: A build tree (here build/, chosen with -B) separate from the source tree (chosen with -S); several build trees with different settings can share one source tree.
source: D1 of F2-26, R6 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Rebuilding only what changed and what depends on it.
analogy: Remaking the tomato sauce and the dishes that use it, nothing else.
precise: A build in which each output is regenerated only if one of its recorded inputs is newer than it; in this build, touching src/stats.cpp recompiled that one file and relinked the library and both programs.
source: D3 of F2-26, R3 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A file listing the exact compiler command used for every source file.
analogy: A photocopy of every instruction given to every cook.
precise: Compile_commands.json, written by CMake when CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS is on; it contains "the exact compiler calls for all translation units of the project in machine-readable form".
source: R7 of F2-26, R4 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: CMake's test runner: it runs every test you listed and reports which passed.
analogy: The head chef's tasting round before service.
precise: The test driver shipped with CMake (ctest), which runs the tests declared with add_test after enable_testing() and reports pass or fail per test.
source: R7 of F2-26, R5 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Building and testing every change automatically, the same way every time.
analogy: Every dish checked by the same checklist before it leaves the kitchen, even on a busy night.
precise: The practice of running a scripted, repeatable build and test (here ci.sh: a Debug build with sanitizers and a Release build, each tested) on every change, on a machine other than the developer's.
source: R6 of F2-26, D4 of F2-26 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Any message the compiler prints about your code: an error, a warning or a note.
analogy: Anything the translator writes in the margin.
precise: A message with a location (file:line:column), a kind (error, warning, note) and text; GCC and Clang add the controlling option in brackets, for example [-Wshadow].
source: D1 of F2-27, R1 of F2-27 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A compiler option that switches one warning, or a group of warnings, on or off.
analogy: Telling the translator which kinds of notes you want.
precise: A -W<name> option; -W<name> enables, -Wno-<name> disables; group flags such as -Wall ("Enable most warning messages.") and -Wextra ("Print extra (possibly unwanted) warnings.") enable sets of warnings.
source: R4 of F2-27, D1 of F2-27 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: An option that makes every warning stop the build.
analogy: The head chef's rule: no recipe goes to the cooks while it has margin notes.
precise: GCC and Clang option that turns warnings into errors, so the compile fails; the template's UNI_WERROR option adds it (F2-26).
source: D1 of F2-27, R6 of F2-27 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Declaring a new variable with the same name as one that already exists, so the old one is hidden.
analogy: Two jars labelled "salt" on two shelves; you reach for the wrong one.
precise: A declaration in an inner scope that hides an entity with the same name in an enclosing scope; -Wshadow "Warn[s] when one variable shadows another".
source: R4 of F2-27, D3 of F2-27 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The compiler changing a value from one type to another without you writing it, sometimes losing part of it.
analogy: The translator rounding "2½ cups" to "2 cups" without telling you.
precise: A conversion inserted by the language rules (for example double to int, which drops the fraction, or int to an unsigned type); -Wconversion is described by g++ as "Warn for implicit type conversions that may" (the help line is cut there; the full text is in the manual).
source: R4 of F2-27, D3 of F2-27 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A variable you read before you gave it a value. It holds whatever was in that memory before.
analogy: A jar you never filled, still holding yesterday's leftovers.
precise: An automatic variable read before any value was stored in it; reading such an indeterminate value is undefined behaviour in C++ (F2-23).
source: D3 of F2-27 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Extra data the compiler puts in the program so a debugger can show source lines and variable names instead of raw addresses.
analogy: Labels on every pot and jar, saying which recipe step filled it.
precise: Tables that map machine addresses to files and lines and describe variables and types, produced with -g; on Linux usually in the DWARF format.
source: D3 of F2-28, R2 of F2-28 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Letting the paused program run for exactly one more source line.
analogy: Unfreeze the kitchen for one recipe step, then freeze again.
precise: GDB next ("Step program, proceeding through subroutine calls."), step ("Step program until it reaches a different source line.", entering called functions) and finish ("Execute until selected stack frame returns.").
source: R5 of F2-28 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The list of function calls that led to where the program is now, newest first.
analogy: The chain of orders: the waiter asked the sauce cook, who asked the prep cook, who reached for the empty jar.
precise: GDB: "Print backtrace of all stack frames, or innermost COUNT frames." Frame #0 is the current function, each higher number is its caller.
source: R5 of F2-28, R7 of F2-28 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A message the operating system sends to a program, for example "you touched memory you may not use".
analogy: The fire alarm going off in the kitchen.
precise: An asynchronous notification to a process on POSIX systems; a program that reads an unmapped address receives SIGSEGV and, by default, is terminated.
source: D4 of F2-28, R7 of F2-28 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The crash you get when a program uses a memory address it is not allowed to use.
analogy: Reaching for a shelf that is not there.
precise: The termination caused by SIGSEGV; bash reported it as "Segmentation fault" and the exit status 139 in this build.
source: R6 of F2-28, D4 of F2-28 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A checker the compiler builds into your program, so the program reports its own mistakes while it runs.
analogy: The food-safety inspector at a practice service.
precise: A compiler instrumentation mode, enabled with -fsanitize=<name> in GCC and Clang, with a runtime library that checks operations and prints a report.
source: D1 of F2-29, D2 of F2-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Extra checking code that the compiler adds around your own code.
analogy: The inspector's checklist stapled to every recipe step.
precise: Compiler-inserted code (for example, a check before every memory load and store) that calls into a runtime library; it changes the program's size and speed but not its intended behaviour.
source: D1 of F2-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A separate, smaller area of memory where ASan writes down which bytes of your memory you are allowed to touch.
analogy: A floor plan with every shelf marked "in use" or "off limits".
precise: In ASan, one shadow byte describes 8 application bytes: 00 means all 8 are addressable, 01–07 that only the first 1–7 are, and other values mark kinds of forbidden memory such as heap redzones (fa) and freed memory (fd).
source: R2 of F2-29, D3 of F2-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A small forbidden gap that ASan puts around each block of memory.
analogy: A strip of red tape on the counter around each tray: touching it is a violation.
precise: Poisoned bytes placed by ASan's allocator before and after each allocation, so that an access right past the end lands in poisoned memory (legend: "Heap left redzone: fa").
source: R2 of F2-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Using memory after it has been given back.
analogy: Reaching into a pan that was already washed and put away.
precise: A read or write through a pointer or reference to a heap block that has been deallocated; undefined behaviour; ASan reports it with the stacks of the access, the free and the allocation.
source: R9 of F2-29, D5 of F2-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: When a container changes, pointers, references and iterators to its elements can stop being valid.
analogy: The restaurant moves the spice rack to a bigger shelf; your note "third jar from the left on the old shelf" now points at nothing.
precise: Rules in the C++ standard library that say which operations invalidate which references; for std::vector, an insertion that exceeds the capacity reallocates storage and invalidates all of them.
source: D5 of F2-29, R9 of F2-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A tool that runs an unchanged program inside a simulator that checks every memory access.
analogy: Inspecting through a camera instead of standing in the kitchen: no change to the cooks, but everything slower.
precise: Valgrind's default tool, "a memory error detector" (its banner); it needs no recompilation, but runs the program on a synthetic CPU.
source: R3 of F2-29, D4 of F2-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One situation you check: an input and the result you expect.
analogy: "the sauce, tasted for salt".
precise: A named check or group of checks with given inputs and expected outputs; in uni_test.h, one UNI_TEST function containing one or more CHECKs.
source: R2 of F2-30, D1 of F2-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The small framework that finds your tests, runs them and reports the result.
analogy: The tasting station with clean spoons and a checklist.
precise: Code that registers test cases, runs them (optionally filtered), reports pass or fail per case, and returns an exit code; uni_test.h is 82 lines and returns 0 only if at least one test ran and none failed.
source: R1 of F2-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Writing a failing test first, then the code that makes it pass, then tidying up.
analogy: Deciding how the sauce must taste before you cook it.
precise: A practice of short cycles "red" (a new test fails), "green" (the simplest code that passes), "refactor" (improve the code with tests still passing).
source: D1 of F2-30, R3 of F2-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A test added after a bug, so the same bug can never come back unnoticed.
analogy: After a customer found a bone, "check for bones" is added to every tasting.
precise: A test that reproduces a fixed defect and is kept in the suite to detect its reintroduction (a "regression").
source: D1 of F2-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: How much of your code the tests actually ran.
analogy: Which pots the tasting spoon has been in at least once.
precise: A measurement by an instrumented build; line coverage is the share of executable lines run at least once; GCC's --coverage and gcov report "Lines executed: …% of N".
source: R5 of F2-30, D2 of F2-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Each test must work the same whether it runs alone, first, last or with others.
analogy: A clean spoon for every tasting.
precise: The property that no test depends on state left by another (global variables, files, environment); tests that break it pass or fail depending on order.
source: R7 of F2-30, R8 of F2-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A system that keeps every saved version of your files, with who changed what, when and why.
analogy: The recipe book where no page is ever erased.
precise: Software that records snapshots of a set of files as a history, so any version can be restored, compared or combined; git is a distributed version control system: every copy holds the whole history.
source: D1 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A project folder plus its full history.
analogy: The whole recipe book, all pages.
precise: In git, the working files plus a .git directory holding objects (file contents, folder listings, commits) and references (branches, tags).
source: D1 of F2-31, R8 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The list of changes you have chosen to put in the next commit.
analogy: The tray of corrected recipe cards waiting to be bound into the book.
precise: Git's index; git add copies the current content of files into it; git status --short shows A for added and ?? for untracked files.
source: R1 of F2-31, D2 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One saved snapshot of the whole project, with a message.
analogy: A new dated page in the recipe book.
precise: A git object that names a tree (the snapshot), zero or more parent commits, an author, a committer, times and a message.
source: R8 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The long hexadecimal name of a commit, computed from its content.
analogy: A fingerprint of the page: change one letter and the fingerprint changes.
precise: The SHA-1 hash (40 hex digits; abbreviated to 7 in --oneline) of the object's type, size and content; in this build git hash-object of hello\n equalled sha1sum of blob 6\0hello\n.
source: R8 of F2-31, D3 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A named line of work, so you can try something without disturbing the main version.
analogy: A test kitchen working on a copy of a recipe.
precise: A movable reference to a commit; a new commit on a branch moves it forward.
source: D1 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Combining the work of two branches.
analogy: Copying the test kitchen's improvements into the main recipe book.
precise: Creating a commit with two parents whose tree combines the changes made on both sides since their common ancestor.
source: R6 of F2-31, R8 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: When two branches changed the same lines differently, and git cannot decide which to keep.
analogy: Two chefs rewrote the same step in different ways; the head chef must choose.
precise: A merge stops with CONFLICT (content), writes both versions between <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>> markers, and waits for you to edit, git add and commit.
source: R6 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Letting git find the commit that broke something by testing the commit halfway, then halfway again.
analogy: Opening the recipe book in the middle of the suspect month and tasting that version.
precise: Git bisect does a binary search between a known good and a known bad commit; git bisect run <script> runs a script at each step, treating exit status 0 as good and other statuses as bad.
source: R4 of F2-31, D2 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Undoing an old commit by adding a new commit that does the opposite.
analogy: A new page that says "go back to the old stock", instead of tearing out a page.
precise: Git revert creates a commit applying the inverse of a given commit's changes; history is kept.
source: R5 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A permanent name for one commit, such as a milestone.
analogy: A bookmark labelled "the version we served at the opening".
precise: A reference to an object that does not move; an annotated tag (git tag -a) is itself an object with a message.
source: R7 of F2-31, D2 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A full copy of a repository, history included.
analogy: A second complete recipe book for a second kitchen.
precise: Git clone copies all objects and creates a working tree from the default branch.
source: R7 of F2-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The chain of "this template was used from there" lines that leads from an error inside a library back to your own code.
analogy: The translator's note "this problem comes from step 9 of your recipe".
precise: When an error occurs inside a template instantiation, GCC prints "In instantiation of …" and "required from …" lines, ending with "required from here" at the user's code; Clang prints "note: in instantiation of … requested here".
source: R1 of F2-32, R3 of F2-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The compiler's translation of your code into processor instructions, as readable text.
analogy: The translated recipe the cooks really follow.
precise: The output of -S (stop after generating assembly); x86-64 assembly is printed in AT&T syntax by default in GCC and Clang, or Intel syntax with -masm=intel.
source: D1 of F2-32, R5 of F2-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The compiler replacing an expensive operation with a cheaper one that gives the same result.
analogy: "divide into 8" becomes "halve three times".
precise: An optimisation that replaces, for example, division by a power of two with a shift (plus a correction for signed values), or a multiplication with additions and shifts.
source: D6 of F2-32, R4 of F2-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Turning a mangled symbol back into the readable C++ name.
analogy: Decoding the jar's label.
precise: Done by c++filt, by nm -C, and by debuggers and sanitizers when they print function names.
source: R6 of F2-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Messages in which the compiler tells you what it optimised, and what it could not, and why.
analogy: The translator's note "I combined steps 3 and 4; I could not combine 7 and 8 because 8 needs 7's result".
precise: GCC -fopt-info-<group>-<kind> (for example -fopt-info-vec-optimized), Clang -Rpass=, -Rpass-missed= and -Rpass-analysis= remarks.
source: R7 of F2-32, R8 of F2-32, D1 of F2-32, D2 of F2-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A tool that measures where a program spends its time or work, function by function.
analogy: The helper with a stopwatch and a tally sheet at every station.
precise: A tool that attributes a cost (time, samples, executed instructions, cache misses) to functions or source lines of a running program.
source: D1 of F2-33, D2 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The small part of a program where most of the time goes.
analogy: The butter-unwrapping station.
precise: A function or loop with a large share of a profile's total cost; in this chapter's first profile, parse_line had 60.82 % of the executed instructions.
source: R3 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The time that passes on a clock on the wall while the program runs.
analogy: How long the customer waits.
precise: Elapsed real time, including time spent waiting or running other programs; measured here with std::chrono::steady_clock and bash's time (%R).
source: R1 of F2-33, R6 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A profiler that looks at what the program is doing many times per second and counts what it sees.
analogy: The helper glancing at the kitchen every few seconds and making a tally mark at whichever station is busy.
precise: A profiler that interrupts the program at intervals and records the current function; gprof printed "Each sample counts as 0.01 seconds".
source: R4 of F2-33, D2 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A profiler that counts every machine instruction the program executes, per function.
analogy: Counting every movement of every cook instead of timing them.
precise: Callgrind runs the program on Valgrind's synthetic CPU and counts executed instructions ("Ir", instructions read); the counts are repeatable but are not times.
source: R3 of F2-33, D1 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The cost of a function including everything it calls.
analogy: The time of the whole fish course, including the sauce made for it.
precise: In callgrind, --inclusive=yes attributes to each function its own instructions plus those of its callees; main is close to 100 %.
source: R3 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The cost of a function's own code only, not the functions it calls.
analogy: The time the fish cook spends with her own hands.
precise: Also called exclusive cost; gprof's "self seconds" column and callgrind's default listing; in the queue profile, self cost was attributed by source file, showing basic_string.h code inlined into take_oldest.
source: R7 of F2-33, R4 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Work that grows with the square of the input: twice as much input, four times as much work.
analogy: Every new ticket makes the cook move every waiting ticket one place along.
precise: Running time proportional to n2 (written O(n2)); recognisable by a factor of about 4 when n doubles.
source: D4 of F2-33, R6 of F2-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)
